prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your New Desktop Companion", "Select a pet personality and visual style that fits your daily workflow."]
1: ["Quick Desktop Controls", "Learn how to summon, minimize, or chat with your new pet anytime."]
2: ["Your pet state, customization, and settings are securely backed up to your account."]
3: ["Preparing Your Companion", "We are generating your pet's desktop animations. We will alert you as soon as it is ready."]
4: ["Use a clear, well-lit frontal photo for best pet generation results.", "Photo Quality Check"]
5: ["Choose Your Adoption Experience", "Pick a ready-to-play pet companion or build a unique custom pet."]
6: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Desktop!", "Check your taskbar or tray icon if your pet overlay does not display immediately."]
7: ["Completing your adoption certificate finishes registration and unlocks your desktop pet."]
8: ["Create Your Companion Account", "Sign in now to save your pet customization, track adoption progress, and sync across devices."]
9: ["Reward Unlocked: Free Desktop Pet Toy Pack"]

verdicts.problem: Requests a personal photo of the user.
